newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi business studies foreign dealing in bourse.
newsitem.headline: Saudi business studies foreign dealing in bourse.

text.p: The Riyadh Chamber of Commerce and Industry said on Wednesday it was looking into the possibility of allowing foreign residents in Saudi Arabia to invest in its stock market -- the biggest in the Gulf.
"We are currently studying this aspect and the study is expected to be over in two months," said a chamber official, speaking by telephone from Riyadh.

"The study is a comparative one and looks at the experiences of some Gulf Arab countries and those of Jordan, Morocco and Tunisia in allowing foreign investment in their stock exchanges," he explained, but would not give details.
The market, capitalised at some $42 billion, is currently restricted to Saudis and other Gulf Arabs.

Saudi newspapers said the move could help foreigners -- who make up six million of the 18 million people in the kingdom -- keep some of their savings in Saudi Arabia and boost the bourse, where business has been sluggish in recent years.
One suggestion, they said, could allow foreign residents to trade in shares through funds managed by Saudi banks.
